transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Tremblay, thank you for coming back in. I have your daughter's chart here and I need to discuss a mistake that was made during the vaccinations earlier.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. We gave your daughter a dose of one of the vaccines that was intended for a child in a higher weight bracket. Essentially, she received more of the medication than was required for her specific weight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How much more?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was the dose for the next weight band up. I was responsible for the drawing of the medication and I selected the wrong one.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is she going to have a reaction? My husband is already stressed about her fever from the last round.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't need you to understand. I need to know if she is in danger right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring her and there are no immediate contraindications, but the dose was technically an overdose for her size.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An overdose. Right. So what happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are just keeping an eye on her for any unusual symptoms today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Unusual symptoms like what? Give me a list.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Fever, redness, or maybe some lethargy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a list. That's a general description. Is this going to affect her long-term health?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is unlikely to cause long-term issues.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a yes or a no.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give a definitive yes or no, but based on the pharmacology, the risk of permanent harm is very low.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is incredibly frustrating. We trust you people with our kids.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not just frustrated. I'm questioning why the system allows a resident to just pick the wrong dose. Was there no double-check?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The weight-based dosing is integrated into our electronic system, but the manual draw was where the error occurred.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you just grabbed the wrong vial.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What is the plan to make sure this doesn't happen to the next kid?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will be reviewing the incident with the department.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan for my daughter. What is the plan for her?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how she responds over the next twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is a vague answer. Do I need to take her to the ER if she gets a fever?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just call the clinic first.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I hear from you about whether this dose needs to be countered or if we need to adjust future shots?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure on the timeline for that yet. I'll have to check with the attending.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are the one who gave it. You should know the next step.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll find out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a written record of exactly which vaccine was overdosed and by how many milligrams. When can I have that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can probably get that to you in a few days. Maybe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need it today. I'm active duty. I don't have time to be chasing a doctor for a mistake they made.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're upset.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not upset, I'm focused on the facts. What are the facts of the recovery plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, we just monitor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. That's a hope.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just stay tuned for any updates from the pharmacy side.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unacceptable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize again for the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Your apology doesn't fix the dose in her system.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is the supervisor here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Dr. Miller is the attending on call.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Get Dr. Miller in here. Now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can check if he's available.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Don't check if he's available. Get him.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish turns and remains regulated despite significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and early, but the resident never performed a comprehension check.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language and explicitly took personal responsibility ('I selected the wrong one') without deflection.

R.justification: The resident relied on generic validation ('I understand', 'I can see you're upset') without naming specific emotions or engaging deeply with the patient's content.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders and vague responses ('we'll see', 'stay tuned', 'I'll find out') without specific timelines or a concrete recovery plan.
